title: Fit a balsa glider's wing through the slot in its body, centred and square, then leave the glider on the table
instruction: Fit the wing through the glider's body, centred and square, and leave the glider on the table.
context: Putting together a dime-store balsa glider is a common childhood job: Guillow's has made them in Wakefield, Massachusetts, for 100 years, and the No. 30 Jetfire is 'no glue required, slot and tab'. The 2 mm wing must meet a slot only 0.8 mm taller than it, slide through flat, and stop centred and square by eye; levered in the slot, it splits the balsa, and a wing left off-centre or crooked makes the glider turn.
setup: Units cm, kg; x forward from the arm bases, y left; heights from the table top (74.75 cm up). Task objects: Guillow's Jetfire No. 30 balsa glider, tailplane and nose clip already on, wing off. Body: balsa profile 28 long x 3.4 tall (6.4 at the fin) x 0.32 thick; tailplane 12 x 4 x 0.16 through its tail slot, flush with the body's lower edge; red plastic nose clip; 0.005 in all. It stands on its lower edge and tailplane along x, nose away from the arms, its wing slot (9.5 long x 0.28 tall, bottom 0.7 above the lower edge) centred at (30, 10). Wing: flat balsa plate 30.5 span, 7.5 root chord tapering to 4.5 at the tips, 0.2 thick, straight trailing edge, 0.004, flat on the table printed side up, trailing edge towards the arms, root-chord centre at (30, -13.5), turned 6 degrees anticlockwise. Distractors, ignored by scoring (SimReady): ceramic mug 11.4 x 9 x 8, 0.30, at (50, 24) yaw 2.4 rad; notebook 22.9 x 17 x 1, 0.12, at (53, -20) yaw 0.25 rad; thin blue marker 10.9 x 0.8, 0.01, at (47, 2) yaw 1.2 rad.
scoring: 0 if the slot has ever cracked: the balsa strip under the wing slot split from the slot's ends (in simulation, the slot wedged open more than 0.5 mm, about 4 N). Through: the wing's centre line crosses the body's mid-plane inside the wing slot (within 3 mm of its ends, 2 mm of its top and bottom), at least 5 mm in from either wing tip. Offset: the wing's centre from the body's mid-plane, along the span (half the difference of the two tip overhangs measured from the body's sides). Out of square: the angle, seen from above, between the wing's span and the perpendicular to the body. 1.0: through, offset at most 3 mm, out of square at most 3 degrees, the glider standing on the table (lower edge within 3 mm of it, tilted at most 10 degrees), glider and wing still, every fingertip at least 3 cm from glider and wing, all held 1 s; full credit lapses if the slot cracks or the wing or glider leaves these tolerances. 0.5: through, offset at most 10 mm and out of square at most 8 degrees, without the rest of 1.0. 0.25: through, further off-centre or out of square than that. 0 otherwise (the wing not through the slot).
reset_notes: Slide the wing back out, lay it flat on its tape marks, and stand the glider on its tape marks. A glider whose slot has split is replaced (about $5).
fidelity: Glider and wing are custom rigid meshes at the Jetfire's listed 12 in span; body thickness, chords, slot size and masses are estimates (no published drawing). The wing is a flat rigid plate: its built-in dihedral and flex are not modelled. The slot's give is one sprung strip (8 N/mm); a crack is that strip forced 0.5 mm open (about 4 N), an estimate, not measured. The slot grips nothing (no preload). Tailplane and nose clip are fixed to the body. Distractors are SimReady props.
